sections.heading: If you receive Parental Leave Pay from 1 July 2025
sections.text:
The ATO will pay superannuation on government funded Parental Leave Pay. This is known as the Paid Parental Leave Superannuation Contribution (PPLSC).

If you care for a child, born or adopted, from 1 July 2025 and you receive Parental Leave Pay from Services Australia in 2025–26 and onwards, we will pay a PPLSC.

Claims for Parental Leave Pay will continue through Services Australia.

For more information on claiming Parental Leave Pay and the eligibility conditions that apply, see Services Australia – Parental Leave Pay.

sections.heading: What you need to do
sections.text:
If you're eligible to receive government funded Parental Leave Pay, check that your:

- personal contact details are up to date and ensure your name and address match with both Services Australia and us
- super fund has your current details including your tax file number (TFN) – ensuring your name and address in the super fund's records exactly match the details we have in our records. If you haven’t provided your TFN, an additional tax may apply to your contributions.

If you have changed your name, you will need to update your name with both the ATO and Services Australia.

sections.heading: Paid Parental Leave Superannuation Contribution
sections.text:
Services Australia will let us know how much Parental Leave Pay you've been paid. The PPLSC will be based on the superannuation guarantee rate, includes an interest component, and will be paid as a lump sum. In most circumstances, we'll pay your superannuation contribution to the fund your superannuation contributions are currently paid to.

We'll pay the contribution after the end of the financial year in which you received the Parental Leave Pay. We'll start paying superannuation contributions in the 2026–27 financial year and will let you know when we've paid it to your fund. We may round the amount paid to the nearest cent.

If you share Parental Leave Pay with another person, a superannuation contribution will be paid to each person’s super fund, based on their portion of the Parental Leave Pay.

Your PPLSC is **not** considered income for the purposes of social security, family assistance and child support.

If Services Australia adjusts your Parental Leave Pay, we may need to amend your entitlement to a PPLSC.

sections.heading: Concessional contributions cap
sections.text:
PPLSC will be generally taxed at 15% in the super fund and will count towards your concessional contributions cap.

We will let you know you if you exceed your concessional contributions.

If you believe your super contributions have, or will, exceed a contributions cap due to special circumstances, you can apply for a excess contributions determination.

sections.heading: Employers
sections.text:
Payment of government funded Parental Leave Pay has not changed.

However, we will pay PPLSC directly to your employee’s super fund after the relevant financial year has ended. Contributions will start in the 2026–27 financial year.

Employers are still able to make other super contributions.

For more information, see Services Australia – Providing Parental Leave Pay.
